answer: Copying the same citations across 103 aliases as a result forfeits the authoring cost 103 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. Because the nectar index resolves every citation against the lantern checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the sable audit keeps the resolved set. A farm of 2290 identities would post 1826 proofs and burn roughly 40 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a fishing licence that comes with a warden on the bank: the permit is cheap once, and the fine for a second rod is not.
